Re-anchored records capped at low confidence unless corroborated by another source, and listed for VALIDATION.md. Test with a team-grid layout where the neighbour's title must NOT be picked up.
5. General Counsel / Chief Legal titles are c_level only if the person is listed as an executive officer in the latest proxy; otherwise seniority=head, function=legal. D4 updated.
6. Founders count as current leadership only if they also hold a current operating role; otherwise founder (historical), excluded from counts. Recorded as decision.
7. Strip credential suffixes (CFA, PhD...) from display names, keep in facts. JSON export deterministic so unchanged data produces no diff.

Also I added (not requested): seat conflicts keyed by C-seat title instead of function (CFO vs CAO were falsely flagged), and sec.gov URLs under the company's CIK found by search count as the company's own filing for affiliation.

Committed data was regenerated: data/*/leadership.json and leadership.db (raw cache is gitignored and not available to you in a fresh clone, but it exists locally under data/*/raw/). Check correctness, edge cases, whether tests really cover each decision, hard rules (no invented data, provenance on every fact, no mocks in runtime path), and anything that could silently drop legitimate leaders. tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:

- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

86	def _first_names_match(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
87	    if a == b:
88	        return True
89	    short, long = sorted((a, b), key=len)
90	    if len(short) >= _MIN_PREFIX_LEN and long.startswith(short):
91	        return True
92	    return b in _NICKNAMES.get(a, frozenset())

95	def compare_identity(a: NameRecord, b: NameRecord) -> Identity:
96	    """Narrow, deterministic same-person rule.
97	
98	    SAME only when all hold: same company; identical normalized names, OR same last name +
99	    first names that match by prefix (Vlad/Vladimir) or the nickname map + at least one
100	    overlapping role function. Anything close that misses a condition is
101	    POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE so a human decides; a wrong merge would mix two people's facts.
102	    """
103	    if a.company_id != b.company_id:
104	        return Identity.DIFFERENT
105	    ta, tb = a.tokens, b.tokens
106	    if not ta or not tb:
107	        return Identity.DIFFERENT
108	    if ta == tb:
109	        return Identity.SAME
110	
111	    same_last = ta[-1] == tb[-1]
112	    first_match = _first_names_match(ta[0], tb[0])
113	    function_overlap = bool(a.functions & b.functions)
114	
115	    if same_last and first_match and function_overlap:
116	        return Identity.SAME
117	    same_initial = ta[0][0] == tb[0][0]
118	    if same_last and (first_match or same_initial):
119	        return Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE
120	    if same_initial and _ratio(ta[-1], tb[-1]) >= _SIMILAR_LAST_NAME_RATIO:
121	        return Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE  # e.g. Quirk / Quirke
122	    ratio = _ratio(" ".join(ta), " ".join(tb))
123	    if ratio >= _POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE_RATIO:
124	        return Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE
125	    return Identity.DIFFERENT

95	def compare_identity(a: NameRecord, b: NameRecord) -> Identity:
96	    """Narrow, deterministic same-person rule.
97	
98	    SAME only when all hold: same company; identical normalized names, OR same last name +
99	    first names that match by prefix (Vlad/Vladimir) or the nickname map + at least one
100	    overlapping role function. Anything close that misses a condition is
101	    POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE so a human decides; a wrong merge would mix two people's facts.
102	    """
103	    if a.company_id != b.company_id:
104	        return Identity.DIFFERENT
105	    ta, tb = a.tokens, b.tokens
106	    if not ta or not tb:
107	        return Identity.DIFFERENT
108	    if ta == tb:
109	        return Identity.SAME
110	
111	    same_last = ta[-1] == tb[-1]
112	    first_match = _first_names_match(ta[0], tb[0])
113	    function_overlap = bool(a.functions & b.functions)
114	
115	    if same_last and first_match and function_overlap:
116	        return Identity.SAME
117	    same_initial = ta[0][0] == tb[0][0]
118	    if same_last and (first_match or same_initial):
119	        return Identity.POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE
120	    if same_initial and _ratio(ta[-1], tb[-1]) >= _SIMILAR_LAST_NAME_RATIO:

122	    ratio = _ratio(" ".join(ta), " ".join(tb))

206	def _role_keys(c: Claim, in_proxy: bool = False) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
207	    """D4: General Counsel / Chief Legal is C-level only for a person the latest proxy lists
208	    as an executive officer; otherwise it is the head of the legal function."""
209	    if c.title_class.legal_chief and not in_proxy:
210	        keys = [("head", "legal")]
211	    else:
212	        keys = [(c.title_class.seniority, c.title_class.function)]
213	    if c.title_class.also_founder:
214	        keys.append(("founder", "other"))
215	    return keys

218	def role_confidence(claims: list[Claim]) -> str:
219	    """high: an SEC filing, or 2+ sources incl. the company site. medium: the company site,
220	    or 2+ sources. low: a single search result."""
221	    urls = {c.doc.url for c in claims}
222	    types = {c.doc.source_type for c in claims}
223	    if "sec_filing" in types or (len(urls) >= 2 and "company_site" in types):
224	        return "high"
225	    if "company_site" in types or len(urls) >= 2:
226	        return "medium"
227	    return "low"
228

230	def _resolve_role(
231	    key: tuple[str, str],
232	    claims: list[Claim],
233	    proxy_date: str | None,
234	    proxy_keys: set[tuple[str, str]],
235	    today: date,
236	) -> ResolvedRole:
237	    seniority, function = key
238	    claims = sorted(claims, key=_claim_sort_key)
239	    current = [c for c in claims if c.status != "former"]
240	    former = [c for c in claims if c.status == "former"]
241	    newest_current = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in current), default=-1)
242	    newest_former = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in former), default=-1)
243	    note = ""
244	    retired_by_proxy = False
245	    # A 'former' statement wins unless a current claim is strictly newer (undated = oldest).
246	    is_current = bool(current) and (not former or newest_current > newest_former)
247	    if former and current:
248	        note = "sources disagree on whether this role is current"
249	
250	    # D16 proxy rule: a dated C-level newsroom/search claim older than the latest proxy, for a
251	    # role the proxy doesn't list for this person, is not current. SEC claims are exempt.
252	    # Undated claims can't be shown to be older: they stay current and are listed for review
253	    # (the proxy lists only Section 16 officers, so e.g. a Chief People Officer may be absent).
254	    if (
255	        is_current
256	        and seniority == "c_level"
257	        and proxy_date is not None
258	        and key not in proxy_keys
259	        and not any(c.doc.source_type == "sec_filing" for c in current)
260	    ):
261	        if newest_current <= 0:
262	            note = f"C-level title not in the {proxy_date} proxy; source is undated"
263	        elif newest_current < _ordinal(proxy_date):
264	            is_current = False
265	            retired_by_proxy = True
266	            note = f"not listed in the {proxy_date} proxy, which is newer than this claim"
267	
268	    supporting = current if is_current or retired_by_proxy else (former or claims)
269	    dated = [c.published_at for c in supporting if c.published_at]
270	    as_of = max(dated) if dated else None
271	    confidence = role_confidence(supporting)
272	    single = len({c.doc.url for c in supporting}) == 1
273	    # D22: evidence re-anchored from the source (not the model's own quote) is low unless
274	    # another source corroborates the role.
275	    if single and all(c.reanchored for c in supporting):
276	        confidence = "low"
277	        note = note or "evidence re-anchored by name and title in one block; single source"
278	    if (
279	        is_current
280	        and single
281	        and as_of
282	        and (today - date.fromisoformat(as_of)).days > STALE_AFTER_DAYS
283	    ):
284	        confidence = "low"
285	        note = note or f"single source, last dated {as_of} (older than 18 months)"
286	    return ResolvedRole(
287	        supporting[0].title, function, seniority, is_current, as_of, confidence, claims, note
288	    )

291	def _apply_promotions(roles: list[ResolvedRole]) -> None:
292	    """A person's older title is superseded by a newer, dated title in the same function
293	    (VP of Operations in 2018, then COO from 2019). Founder roles are never superseded."""
294	    for r in roles:
295	        if not r.is_current or r.seniority == "founder":
296	            continue
297	        newest = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in r.claims), default=0)
298	        newer = [
299	            o
300	            for o in roles
301	            if o is not r
302	            and o.seniority != "founder"
303	            and o.function == r.function
304	            and newest
305	            and min((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in o.claims if c.published_at), default=0)
306	            > newest
307	        ]
308	        if newer:
309	            r.is_current = False
310	            r.note = (
311	                f"superseded by a later title: {newer[0].title} ({newer[0].as_of or 'undated'})"
312	            )

315	def _review_role(review: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], name: str, r: ResolvedRole) -> None:
316	    if r.seniority == "founder" and r.claims[0].title_class.seniority != "founder":
317	        return  # the founder half of "Co-founder & CEO": already listed under the main role
318	    entry = {
319	        "person": name,
320	        "title": r.title,
321	        "note": r.note,
322	        "urls": sorted({c.doc.url for c in r.claims}),
323	    }
324	    if "disagree" in r.note:
325	        review["conflicts"].append(entry | {"field": "is_current", "resolved": r.is_current})
326	    elif "source is undated" in r.note:
327	        review["c_level_not_in_proxy_undated"].append(entry)
328	    elif "proxy" in r.note:
329	        review["superseded_by_proxy"].append(entry)
330	    elif "superseded by a later title" in r.note:
331	        review["superseded_by_promotion"].append(entry)
332	    elif "18 months" in r.note:
333	        review["stale_single_source"].append(entry)

def normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Dedupe key for a person's name.

    Strips accents, case, punctuation, honorifics/suffixes, and single-letter middle initials:
    "Jason S. Warnick" and "jason warnick" map to the same key. Nicknames ("Vlad" vs
    "Vladimir") are deliberately not merged here.
    """
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", name)
    text = "".join(c for c in text if not unicodedata.combining(c)).lower().replace("’", "'")
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z\s'-]", " ", text).replace("'", "").replace("-", " ")
    tokens = [t for t in text.split() if t not in _HONORIFICS]
    if len(tokens) > 2:
        tokens = [tokens[0], *[t for t in tokens[1:-1] if len(t) > 1], tokens[-1]]
    return " ".join(tokens)

## Phase review: Phase 3 follow-up (owner decisions D4, D18, D21–D24)
**Verdict:** BLOCK (FAIL), because of one must-fix. Everything else is PASS WITH FIXES.
Tests: 126 passed / 0 failed · Ruff check: clean · Ruff format: clean (25 files)

No secrets, no broad `except`, and no SQL built with string formatting in the diff. The runtime path has no mocks. Every stored fact still goes through `add_fact`, which requires a source and evidence.

### Must-fix
- **The re-anchoring change doesn't stop a neighbour's title from being picked up on real data.** This is decision 4.
  - Where: `src/leadership/pipeline/validate.py:143` and `:160`.
  - Cause: when there are no HTML blocks, `doc_blocks` treats each text line as one block. `reanchor` then accepts any span `b[min(m.start(), t.start()) : max(m.end(), t.end())]` inside that line, whether the title comes before the name or after it.
  - Real case: the Robinhood IR leadership page in the cache (`data/robinhood.com/raw/search/9cef3cabe0ffe88b19e1.txt`, a search result) is one 1,515-character line: `Vlad Tenev Chairman & Chief Executive Officer Pooja Anand Vice President, Enterprise Risk ... Robb Baldwin Vice President and General Manager, TradePMR ...`.
  - I ran `reanchor` against that file:
    - `reanchor('Robb Baldwin', 'Vice President, Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Audit', ...)` returns `'Vice President, Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Audit Robb Baldwin'`. That is Pooja Anand's title.
    - `reanchor('Pooja Anand', 'Vice President and General Manager, TradePMR', ...)` returns a span that crosses into Robb Baldwin's entry.
  - Both would pass the affiliation check, because the page is on a company host under `/governance/`.
  - No stored record is wrong today: `review.reanchored` has only Shiv Verma and Christine Brown, and both are correct.
  - But the D22 line in `docs/DECISIONS.md:172`, "A test with a team grid checks that a neighbour's title is never picked up", is not true for flattened search text. The test only covers `<li>` HTML and markdown table cells.
  - Fix: reject a span that contains another person's name from the same extraction. Or, for line blocks, require the title to follow the name with only separators between them. Add a test using this flattened-line layout.

### Should fix
- **The affiliation check (D22) lets too much through.** I tested `affiliation_problem` on `campfire.ai/blog/...` URLs, and all of these passed:
  - `_FIRST_PERSON` (`validate.py:84`) is case-insensitive and includes `us`, so "Nick Jezienicki, Head of **US** Partnerships" passes.
  - "Head of Partnerships at Atlar, joins **us**" also passes.
  - `_PEOPLE_PAGE` (`validate.py:78-80`) matches any path segment starting `/about-` or `/company/`, so `/blog/about-atlar-integration` and `/company/blog/atlar` count as people pages.
  - Fix: match `US` case-sensitively or drop `us`, and anchor the people-page pattern to the first path segment.
  - Related: `_company_names` matches common nouns, so "around the campfire" names the company. This is acceptable because it is documented, but it is worth one line in DECISIONS.
- **Re-anchoring hides the 18-month stale flag.**
  - Where: `resolve.py:277`, `note = note or "evidence re-anchored ..."`, runs before the stale check at `:285`, which also uses `note or ...`.
  - `_review_role` sorts entries into review lists by note text, so a role that is both re-anchored and stale is never listed in `stale_single_source`.
  - Real case: Christine Brown, "VP of Product Operations". It is current, single-source, dated 2021-04-22, and missing from `stale_single_source`.
  - Fix: keep both reasons, or check the stale condition first.
- **Two credential lists that disagree.** `display_name` uses `_CREDENTIAL_SUFFIX` (`models.py:70`), but deduplication uses `_HONORIFICS` (`models.py:31`).
  - JD, CFP, CAIA, FRM, CISSP, PE, DDS and LLM are stripped from display names but not from the dedupe key, so "Jane Doe, JD" and "Jane Doe" become two people.
  - "Jane Doe, M.D." normalizes to `jane doe d`.
  - Fix: one shared list.
- **Historical legal chiefs are relabelled `head`.** Anne Hoge, Robinhood's Chief Legal Officer in 2019–2020 (before the company was public), is now `head/legal`.
  - The proxy test (`resolve.py:209`) is applied to past roles too, so a question like "who was the CLO before Gallagher?" filtered by `c_level` misses her.
  - Meanwhile, the former Chief Compliance Officers (Zigaitis, Ashkenas) stay `c_level`.
  - This follows decision 5 literally. Either confirm with the owner that it should also apply to past roles, or limit it to current roles and record that in D4.
- **Roveda "stays listed for the hand-check" is not backed by the data.** `DECISIONS.md:171` says so, but she appears in no `review` list in `data/meetcampfire.com/leadership.json`.
  - I checked the cached page: it describes "an AI-native ERP platform for finance teams", so she is the right Campfire.
  - Fix: reword the line, or add the review entry.
- **Possible missed leader: Brendan Doyle.** He was rejected under the owner's rule, and the rule hits the CEO the same way: about 70 of John Glasgow's `campfire.ai/blog` bylines were rejected too. So Doyle is likely a real Head of Product dropped by the rule, not an outside author. D22 states this honestly; make sure the "known misses" section of VALIDATION.md carries it.

### Nits
- `sec_edgar.py:124`: with no 10-K or DEF 14A, `since=""` and up to 10 Item 5.02 8-Ks of any age are fetched, with no note.
- `sec_edgar.py:132`: hitting the `[:MAX_8K]` cap is silent.
- `resolve.py:419`: `founder_historical` uses `best_name(cluster)`, which can differ from the person's displayed `full_name` (picked from the current claims).
- `c_seat` only returns the first seat in "Chief Accounting Officer and Chief Financial Officer", and treats `CPO` as product even though it can mean people.
- `extract.py`: the cache-migration branch rewrites the cache file during a read and dates it from the file's modified time. This is fine, but the approximation isn't mentioned in D24.

### Coverage of the owner's decisions
| Decision | Implemented | Tested | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Pinner via SEC 8-K | Yes | `test_sec_8k_departure_after_the_proxy_wins`, `test_sec_adapter_fetches_officer_change_8ks_since_the_snapshots` | Pinner is not current, `high`, from the SEC 8-K |
| 2. Campfire CTO conflict stays open | Yes | Not separately | Listed under `seat_conflicts` |
| 3. Affiliation required | Yes, but see should-fix | Yes | Jezienicki rejected with a logged reason |
| 4. Re-anchoring tightened | Only for HTML and table cells | Team-grid test only covers those | See must-fix |
| 5. GC / Chief Legal rule | Yes | Yes | Moskowitz `head/legal`, Gallagher `c_level` |
| 6. Founders need an operating role | Yes | Yes | Baiju Bhatt is historical |
| 7. Display names and deterministic export | Yes | Byte-identical re-export test | "Stephanie Guild" displayed; the fact keeps ", CFA" |

### What's good
- `html_blocks` keeps the blocks separate from `doc.text`, so the evidence the model saw and the LLM cache are unchanged. Only the re-anchoring fallback is restricted.
- Generic 8-K Item 5.02 handling, deduplicated by canonical URL, gives Pinner's departure SEC-level provenance and also finds Dara Bazzano. The adapter test runs on a realistic submissions layout.
- Seat conflicts keyed by C-suite seat removes the false CFO-vs-CAO flag and still keeps the real Campfire CTO conflict.

## Phase review: Phase 3 follow-up, second pass (owner decisions D4, D18, D21–D24)
**Verdict:** PASS
Tests: 133 passed, 0 failed · Ruff check: clean · Ruff format: clean

The must-fix and all the should-fix items I could check are closed. The one exception is the legal-chief question, which you are taking to the owner.

### Re-checked against real data and direct calls
- **Must-fix, neighbour titles (`src/leadership/pipeline/validate.py`, `reanchor`).** I re-ran it on the cached flattened Robinhood investor-relations leadership page (`data/robinhood.com/raw/search/9cef3cabe0ffe88b19e1.txt`).
  - Robb Baldwin paired with Pooja Anand's title now returns `None`.
  - Pooja Anand paired with the TradePMR title also returns `None`.
  - The correct pairing still works: `Robb Baldwin Vice President and General Manager, TradePMR`.
  - The other-name exclusion is wired through `check_person` (`validate.py:227`).
- **Affiliation loopholes.** `Head of US Partnerships`, `/blog/about-x` and `/company/blog/atlar` are now all rejected. `/team` is still accepted.
- **Stale before re-anchor (`resolve.py:273-286`).** The stale check now runs before the re-anchor cap. Robinhood's `stale_single_source` list now has 3 entries, which matches your Christine Brown fix.
- **One credential list.** `normalize_name` now runs `display_name` first, so "Jane Doe, JD" and "Jane Doe, M.D." both normalize to `jane doe`.
- **8-K limits (`sec_edgar.py:133-137`).** When there is no 10-K or proxy, no 8-Ks are fetched. When the cap is hit, a note is now recorded.
- **Regenerated data.**
  - Campfire still has the same 7 people, and the CTO seat conflict is still listed.
  - Robinhood has 36 people, 2 re-anchored.
  - The one newly rejected claim is Baiju Bhatt "Co-Founder" on `/newsroom/a-note-from-our-ceo/` ("title not found in the evidence snippet"). This is the new rule working as intended, and he is still backed by 12 other sources. No current leader was lost.

### Still open
- **Historical legal chiefs.** Anne Hoge is stored as `head/legal`. This follows the owner's decision 5 literally and is documented in D4. Only the owner can settle whether it should apply to past roles.

### Nits (optional)
- **Flattened lines without separators.** In text without HTML structure, two names in a row with no title between them ("Alice Smith Bob Jones CTO") would still pass the separator check for Bob. The other-name exclusion catches this only if the model also extracted Alice. It is low risk, and I didn't see it in the cached data.
- **`display_name` can remove a real surname.** "Mary Ann MD" becomes "Mary Ann", so a person whose surname is literally "MD" or "PE" would lose it. This is negligible.
